summary: Old Baldy lookout on Lookout Mountain, built 1915, replaced in 1927 by a Sunset Peak tower removed in 1974; only footings remain there.

facts.design: Region 5 Plan 4A enclosed timber tower (1915 Lookout Mountain station); later L-4 or BC-301 cab on a steel tower at Sunset Peak
facts.status_note: Both towers are gone. Only footings and a foundation remain on Sunset Peak.
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Angeles National Forest

corrections.why: The record point sits at the Mount San Antonio summit (Wikipedia gives 34°17′20″N 117°38′48″W). The register says no lookout was located there and gives the Lookout Mountain site's coordinates to the southwest.
The register places the Lookout Mountain site in Los Angeles County. Mount San Antonio lies on the county line, so the summit point may be in either county.
The register says the station stood on Lookout Mountain, also known as Old Baldy Lookout, and that no lookout was located on Mt. San Antonio. The Fuego Vista link is only suggested.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Mount San Antonio lies on the Los Angeles and San Bernardino county border; the register puts the Lookout Mountain station in Los Angeles County. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The record's status 'unknown' is superseded: both towers are removed (register). Identity is the main uncertainty: the register only suggests Lookout Mountain is the Fuego Vista site, and the Forest Lookouts page quotes 1915-1927 newspapers and Forest Service items second-hand. Record location and county disagree with the register (see corrections). Sunset Peak is a separate register entry (US 1729, CA 20) and the story treats it as the successor station. Register gives 10,046 ft for Mt. Baldy; Wikipedia gives 10,064 ft; not used in the story. No source describes the Lookout Mountain site today or whether either site is open to visitors, so access is omitted. The 20 ft height fits both towers; the record's 6.1 m is kept for the 1915 station.
